newsitem.title: UK: U.S gasoline fall slams shut Euro mogas arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: U.S gasoline fall slams shut Euro mogas arbitrage.

text.p: Sharp drops in U.S gasoline prices over the last two days have banged shut an arbitrage window that has seen nearly one million tonnes of European material head transatlantic, traders said on Wednesday.
"We cannot move barrels across (transatlantic) because of the drop in gasoline over the last two days," said one trader at a major.
From the end of December until the the beginning of this week the arbitrage opportunity drew nearly one million tones of finished and unfinished gasoline and blending components to the United States.
Traders on Wednesday estimated they would have to pick up European material at around $207.50 to break even on the trip when barges were pegged around $216-217 fob.
Difficulty in securing a tanker on the spot market and the cost of high freight have also scuppered the chances of transatlantic movements.

The chartering on Tuesday by trading house Glencore of the SCF Trader to load 80,000 tonnes from Immingham, U.K. on February 2-4 for a trip to the U.S, may constitute the vanguard of a European fleet totalling nearly 30 U.S.-bound gasoline ships.
